issues.legal_issue: A court may appoint a substitute arbitrator when the designated arbitrator refuses or is unable to act, unless the arbitration agreement shows that the parties intended the vacancy not to be filled.
material_facts: The parties had an arbitration agreement referring disputes to a judicial office-holder as arbitrator.
After disputes arose, the designated arbitrator refused to act, and the parties did not fill the vacancy.
The agreement did not indicate that the parties intended the vacancy to remain unfilled; designating the arbitrator by reference to the office held did not itself show that intention.
issues.conclusion: The agreement did not exclude filling the vacancy, so the court could appoint a new arbitrator. The appeals were allowed, and the cases were remitted for appointment of a substitute arbitrator.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 8(1)(b) of the Arbitration Act, 1940, a court may fill an arbitrator’s vacancy where an appointed arbitrator refuses or is unable to act, the parties have not supplied the vacancy, and the agreement does not show that the parties intended it should not be filled. Silence is presumed to permit filling the vacancy; the agreement must show an intention not to fill it, and merely designating an arbitrator by reference to an office does not establish that intention. Section 20(4) provides for reference to a court-appointed arbitrator where the parties cannot agree upon one. The Court relied on Governor General in Council v. Associated Live Stock Farm (India) Ltd., Union of India v. Rai Narain Misra, and Fertilizer Corporation of India Ltd. v. M/s. Domestic Engineering Installation; it distinguished Chief Engineer, Buildings and Roads v. Harbans Singh and M/s. Isherdass Sahni and Bros. v. Union of India, and disapproved District Co-operative Federation Ltd. v. Khub Chand and Bharat Construction Co. Ltd. v. Union of India.

rule.if: arbitration_vacancy_proceeding and agreement_named_arbitrator and designated_arbitrator_cannot_act and vacancy_remains_unfilled and agreement_does_not_exclude_filling

predicates.arbitration_vacancy_proceeding: A court proceeding concerns referring a dispute under an arbitration agreement to arbitration.
predicates.agreement_named_arbitrator: The parties' agreement designated an arbitrator to resolve their disputes.
predicates.designated_arbitrator_cannot_act: The designated arbitrator refused or was unable to act.
predicates.vacancy_remains_unfilled: The parties did not supply the vacancy after the designated arbitrator ceased to be available.
predicates.agreement_does_not_exclude_filling: The agreement does not show that the parties intended the vacancy to remain unfilled.

issues.definition: When a court proceeding concerns an arbitration vacancy, the agreement designated an arbitrator who cannot act, the parties have left the vacancy unfilled, and the agreement does not exclude filling it, the court may appoint a substitute arbitrator.
